summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with neck and left arm tightness, initially concerning for cardiac ischemia. She had a mildly elevated troponin and transient ST changes, but no acute coronary syndrome was confirmed. A dipyridamole stress test revealed a fixed perfusion defect in the LCx territory, with echocardiogram showing new regional wall motion abnormalities and mild systolic dysfunction. Her symptoms resolved with supportive care. Acute kidney injury was noted with elevated creatinine, improving during the stay. Transplant nephrology optimized immunosuppression with increased tacrolimus and sirolimus due to subtherapeutic levels. Amlodipine was discontinued for hypotension, and she was transitioned from pravastatin to high-intensity atorvastatin. Clopidogrel was added for dual antiplatelet therapy. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up planned in cardiology and transplant nephrology.
